newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine property boom not yet over - experts.
newsitem.headline: Philippine property boom not yet over - experts.

text.p: The boom in the Philippine property sector is expected to be sustained beyond year 2000 due to high demand from multinational companies, improved local infrastructure and increased buying power of Filipinos, property appraiser Cuervo Far East Inc/Richard Ellis company said on Tuesday.

"Contrary to what skeptics foresee as a near-eventual market glut, we expect the Philippine market to even improve well beyond the year 2000," Rick Santos, country representative of the company, said in a statement.

In the office sector, even if a new supply of 2.3 million square metres is projected by the year 2000, an equal demand is expected to come from Hong Kong firms preparing to migrate and globalising companies planning to put up regional headquarters, he said.

"As a matter of fact, major developers responsible for Hong Kong's property success are here. They are studying and preparing for the eventual exit of multinational companies from the Crown colony," he said.
The residential and retail property sector, on the other hand, is expected to be driven by increased buying power and retail trade liberalization, he said.
Santos said the industrial property sector is also on the upswing. "As more infrastructure projects come on line, we expect an even greater influx of foreign manufacturing firms," he said.
